findings.text: Headers use single definition guards to prevent repeated inclusion.
Signal delivery info pairs a user identifier and a process identifier with a trailing variable length security context area that extends the fixed header.

Kernel audit rule stores policy and list selectors plus action, a syscall mask, allocation length, field count, a filter key string, a field array with fast paths for architecture and inode tests, watch and tree and executable markers, two list links for watch or tree membership and for listing, and a numeric priority.
Rule field comparator stores a type tag, a value that may be a raw integer or a user or group identity or a security module string with its compiled rule handle, and an operator code.

Combined status selector aggregates the individual enabled, failure, identifier, rate and backlog controls with loss and actual wait time. Unset inode number and unset device use all bits set sentinels.

Record origin tags distinguish unknown, normal, parent, child delete and child create cases with consecutive small numbers from zero. Inode annotations mark parent, hidden and incomplete evaluation with values one, two and four. Terminal and security configuration use single bit flags for enable, password logging, subject and object context.

Audit enable states are off zero, on one and locked two. Legacy login identifier marker is one. Audit syscall argument capacity is six. Compatibility test either checks the sixty four bit architecture flag or is constantly false in alternate builds. Alternate builds report zero rules, zero signals and disabled state.

Time correction types cover offset, frequency, status, tai, tick and adjust with a trailing count. Filter configuration operations cover classic table families and nftables table, chain, rule, set, element, generation, object and flowtable families with register, unregister, replace and reset variants plus a terminal invalid value. Syscall classes cover native, compat, open, openat, socketcall, execve and openat2 with a trailing count.

Time correction value pairs old and new signed wide integers. Time data in full builds holds one such pair per correction type sized by the count; in alternate builds it is an empty structure with no storage.

Logging interface provides message emit, buffer start, formatted append, close, hex dump, bounded string, untrusted string, path with prefix, key, denied path, subject and object context, task context and info, and packet helpers. In the observed variant emit and formatting are empty, start returns null, and context and packet helpers report zero.

Login user and session accessors either read task stored values or report invalid user and unset session in alternate builds. Enabled state is reported as off, signal info reports zero, and security configuration update is empty in alternate builds.
Login identifier is considered set exactly when the retrieved value passes the validity test.

Task audit context management exposes store, current fetch, dummy test, allocation and release. Allocation in the stub reports success without action. Store writes the context pointer into the task or does nothing. Fetch returns current task context or null. Dummy test reports empty when the pointer is missing or flagged, or constantly true in alternate builds. Release forwards only when a context is present or does nothing.

Event hooks cover uring and syscall boundaries, name and inode and file observation, hidden parent and child relations, process tracing, ipc objects and permissions, descriptor pairs, exec parameters, native and compat socket calls, socket addresses, message queue open and transfer and notify and attributes, exec capabilities, capability sets, mapped descriptors, extended open attributes, kernel module names, fanotify responses, time offset injection, time data init and update and log, netfilter configuration, dumps, seccomp and related actions. Enabled variants delegate to internal handlers; alternate variants are empty or report zero.

Most hooks proceed only when the dummy test is false. Uring entry additionally requires enabled state. Fanotify and netfilter configuration hooks require enabled state alone. Time injection ignores a zero offset. Time init clears storage and setters index by type. Compat socket handling widens narrow arguments into a fixed capacity array bounded by the passed count.

Context lifecycle moves from allocation to association with a task, then per event collection during syscall or uring execution and path or ipc or network activity, then syscall or uring exit finalization, ending with release. Alternate builds collapse all states to no operation with null or dummy context and zero return.

DMA buffer operations table provides optional attach and detach for device compatibility and housekeeping, optional pin and unpin for movement control, and mandatory mapping into device address space with sleepable allocation or migration and attribute handling.

Pin, unpin and dynamic mapping run with the buffer reservation object held. Pin and cached mapping are mutually exclusive, as are unpin and cached mapping. Non dynamic importers are pinned automatically during attach.

Trailing context bytes, nullable log buffers, fixed syscall argument capacity, indexed time and mask arrays, and sleepable DMA mapping impose bounds, null tolerance and calling context requirements on callers.
